facebook.long_form:
Pete Crow-Armstrong enters Sunday sitting at 41 home runs and 36 stolen bases.

The math is simple and the stakes are enormous. He needs 4 more stolen bases in roughly 14 remaining games to join the most exclusive club in baseball: the 40-40 Club. Six players have done it across the entire history of Major League Baseball — Jose Canseco (1988), Barry Bonds (1996), Alex Rodriguez (1998), Alfonso Soriano (2006), Ronald Acuña Jr. (2023), and Shohei Ohtani (2024). PCA would be the seventh. He would also be the first Cub to accomplish it ever, and the first Cubs player to reach 40 home runs in a single season since Derrek Lee did it in 2005.

The question in September is never purely statistical. The Cubs are in a Wild Card race. Managers in pennant chases sometimes pull back the green light for baserunners to avoid injury or outs. Crow-Armstrong will need the Cubs coaching staff to keep trusting him in situations where a steal attempt makes sense — and he'll need the base hits and walks to get there.

With 14 games left, this window is real. A run of 4 steals in two weeks isn't automatic, but it's absolutely within reach for one of the most well-rounded offensive players in the National League.

stories.title: Yordan Alvarez — AL Triple Crown Chase Gets Complicated (Tier 1 | FOLLOW UP)
stories.angle: Alvarez is chasing the rarest individual feat in baseball — the AL Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average (~.310) and is within striking distance in RBI, but Junior Caminero's walk-off home run Saturday kept Caminero at 39 HR (one ahead of Alvarez at 38). Alvarez is the overwhelming AL MVP favorite but the Triple Crown requires leading in all three. With ~14 games left, every category is still up for grabs. Cabrera 2012 was the last AL Triple Crown winner.

facebook.long_form:
Yordan Alvarez is trying to do something that hasn't been done in the American League since Miguel Cabrera in 2012 — win the Triple Crown.

Through the first eight months of the 2026 season, Alvarez leads the American League in batting average (approximately .310). His home run total (38) and RBI total (approximately 96) put him within striking distance in both categories — but Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays hit a walk-off home run on Saturday to stay at 39, one ahead of Alvarez, and the RBI race is similarly tight.

The Triple Crown is defined as leading your league in batting average, home runs, and RBI simultaneously at the end of the season. It requires sustained excellence across three completely different statistical measures, and it is extraordinarily rare in the modern game. Cabrera did it in 2012. Carl Yastrzemski did it in 1967. Before Cabrera, you have to go back decades to find another AL winner.

Alvarez is already the overwhelming AL MVP favorite — his season would be elite regardless of whether he catches Caminero in HR or pulls away in RBI. But the Triple Crown is the category that would separate his 2026 from merely great seasons and put it into historical territory.

14 games remain. Every plate appearance in the next two weeks carries extra weight.

stories.title: Mets 12, Yankees 2 — Subway Series Statement (Tier 2 | NEW)
stories.angle: The Mets dismantled the Yankees 12-2 on Saturday at Yankee Stadium in a subway series blowout that raises questions about a Yankees team still adjusting to Aaron Judge's return from a 99-day IL stint. Judge returned September 8 and is working back to full strength while the Yankees hold a slim Wild Card lead. The Mets, meanwhile, served notice that the NL is not short on firepower.

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Mets 12, Yankees 2. At Yankee Stadium. On a Saturday.

Aaron Judge is back from a 99-day IL absence. The Yankees are still figuring it out. ⚾

#Yankees #LGM

facebook.long_form:
The score was 12-2. The venue was Yankee Stadium. The winner was the Mets.

On Saturday, September 12, the Mets delivered a decisive subway series statement, handling the Yankees by 10 runs on their home field. Aaron Judge returned from his 99-day IL absence on September 8 — he missed that stretch with a stress fracture in his rib — and the Yankees are still working to regain their identity around their superstar.

The Yankees entered Saturday holding a Wild Card spot in the AL. They still hold it. But a 10-run loss at home to a rival in a meaningful September weekend is not the kind of result a playoff-contending team looks forward to filing away. Judge's return has been anticipated all season, and the Yankees clearly need time to re-find their full-season form around him.

For the Mets, the win was a statement — but more specifically, it was the kind of convincing result that earns attention in September and reinforces the message that the National League is not short on capable teams.

stories.angle: Misiorowski leads MLB with a 1.95 ERA. He's 19-8 with 236 strikeouts for the Brewers, and at age 24 he's rewriting expectations for what a second-year starter can do. The Cy Young market has him at -700 while the next contender is well behind. With Milwaukee fighting for playoff positioning, Misiorowski is both a Cy Young lock and the engine driving the Brewers' push. His next start comes in the next few days.

facebook.long_form:
Jacob Misiorowski has a 1.95 ERA.

He's 19-8. He has 236 strikeouts. He is 24 years old. He throws 100 miles per hour on a consistent basis. And he is the most dominant starting pitcher in Major League Baseball in 2026.

The NL Cy Young Award market has him at -700. The next candidate is available at roughly +500. That is not a close race — that is a coronation that is waiting for the final month of the season to make it official.

What makes Misiorowski's 2026 season historically significant isn't just the ERA. It's the combination. A sub-2.00 ERA in the current offensive environment is rare. A 19-8 record means his team has won behind him at a high rate. And 236 strikeouts — with a few weeks still left — projects to one of the highest totals in recent NL history.

He pitches for the Brewers, who are fighting for their own postseason positioning. Every start Misiorowski makes in September carries double significance — it is both a Cy Young vote and a potential playoff win.

stories.title: NL Wild Card — Three Teams In, One Spot Still Open (Tier 2 | FOLLOW UP)
stories.angle: The Phillies dropped a 6-5 gut-punch to the Braves on Saturday (Drake Baldwin walk-off double), which tightens the NL Wild Card picture heading into Sunday. The Cubs and Phillies hold WC1 and WC2. The Padres hold WC3 by a half-game over Arizona. With 14 games left and a Padres-D-backs series at Petco Park Sept 25-27 looming, the final spot could come down to a three-game set in San Diego.

facebook.long_form:
The National League Wild Card picture heading into Sunday:

The Phillies hold one of the top two Wild Card spots alongside the Cubs. The Padres hold the third and final spot. The Arizona Diamondbacks are 0.5 games behind San Diego. 14 games remain.

Saturday was not a good day for Philadelphia. The Braves beat the Phillies 6-5 in 11 innings on a Drake Baldwin walk-off double. The Phillies are still in the field, still in comfortable position — but losses like Saturday's tighten margins and serve as reminders that nothing in September baseball is guaranteed.

The most consequential series on the calendar for the final Wild Card spot comes September 25-27, when the Padres host the Diamondbacks at Petco Park. Three games between the two teams fighting for the same playoff spot, with roughly one week left in the regular season. That series has the potential to decide who goes to the Wild Card round on September 29.
